searchText: Could someone explain why `tip == min(tip, max_base_fee - cur_base_fee)`? Why not simply accept `tip` and if `max_base_fee > cur_base_fee` the tx is not valid? transaction miner fee: 5 miner fee demand: 1 base fee: 100 fee cap: 103 That transaction should go through. <@543900561460822016> why should that tx go through, outside the pathological case? wait, that tx would go through in both cases listed above in the current scenario, the total paid would be 103 in the scenario i am proposing it would be 105 That would violate the user's fee_cap setting. i'm asking why is that in place in the first place? the desire is for the user to set a max amount they'll pay, that can be done in both cases You mean why not have `max_base_fee` instead of `fee_cap`? the max out of pocket cost is either `fee_cap` of `fee_cap + tip` yes exactly I have twice now thought the same as you are thinking and both times spent like a month thinking that way only to be reminded of a thing, that I now cannot remember, that instantly convinced me to abandon that view. I am sad that I once again have forgotten what it was, but glad that I haven't yet again forgotten that it exists! The EIP rationale doesn't mention this (it should)? there actually isn't a rationale section in 1559, so no it isn't mentioned 😦 Ugh, how did that happen? I guess this EIP is a bit old. the eip bot is not yet sentient The only advantage that I can think of in status quo is that there will be a range of txs that continue to be valid, where there is a hard cut off in the latter. Which may seem weird to a user. They may offer a tip of 100, but because their `max_base_fee is < cur_base_fee` the tx is invalid imo this seems like the pathological case though, and i can't see why it would occur in the wild the advantage of allowing the mempool to accept the tip at face value, rather than constantly computing the `min(tip, fee_cap - base_fee)`, is it drastically simplifies the ordering logic for miners From a UX standpoint, I think fee_cap is a bit easier to explain. "Pay whatever base fee is required and up to X to the miner, but never pay more than Y" "Pay whatever base fee is required up to Y, and X to the miner." While the statements are similar complexity in the mathematic sense, I think users internally have a "max willing to pay" function and they don't care how that is divided up so much. ^ i agree with this Hopefully someone else can provide a more compelling argument. I do like the idea of simplifying sorting. imo this is more a problem with communication to users "Pay at most `fee_cap`, if `tip > fee_cap - base_fee` then your tx is less likely to get in because it pays the miner less" "Pay at most `fee_max + tip`, as long as `fee_max > base_fee` your tx will be included proportional to your tip" i think that the second may actually be simpler to reason about as a user, since they generally care about how quickly their tx will be included on-chain we just need to shift the idea from "I'll pay at most X, the network can figure out how to include it" to "I'll pay at most Y+T and I will *always* tip the miner T, because T parameterizes the speed at which i'd like my tx included"

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: Could someone explain why  `tip == min(tip, max_base_fee - cur_base_fee)`? Why not simply accept `tip` and if `max_base_fee > cur_base_fee` the tx is not valid?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
transaction miner fee: 5
miner fee demand: 1
base fee: 100
fee cap: 103

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: That transaction should go through.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: why should that tx go through, outside the pathological case?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: wait, that tx would go through in both cases listed above

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: in the current scenario, the total paid would be 103 in the scenario i am proposing it would be 105

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: That would violate the user's fee_cap setting.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: i'm asking why is that in place in the first place? the desire is for the user to set a max amount they'll pay, that can be done in both cases

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: You mean why not have `max_base_fee` instead of `fee_cap`?

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: the max out of pocket cost is either `fee_cap`  of `fee_cap + tip`

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yes exactly

excerpts.content: I am sad that I once again have forgotten what it was, but glad that I haven't yet again forgotten that it exists!
